new.headline: Cut weekly mileage, keep a hard workout and a long run to stay race ready.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer: I’m not comfortable continuing to run that much more each week. The last week’s volume was a big jump from previous weeks and the high hard‑minute load can lead to fatigue and injury. You should reduce mileage gradually and focus on recovery so you’re fresh for the race.

new.analysis: The athlete pushed far above the prescribed 53‑mile week, adding a long 20‑mile run and extra work that raised hard minutes to 34. Over‑training is unsustainable and risks fatigue before the race. In a build phase the plan must keep the athlete race‑ready while beginning a taper—reduced volume and a controlled hard session. The next week will cut roughly 12 miles from last week, keeping 41 miles total: an easy Tuesday, a single quality workout Wednesday, easy runs Thursday and Saturday, and a long run of 18 miles Sunday at an easy pace. This keeps about 80 % of the week in easy work, with the hard effort concentrated in one quality day and the long run staying in zone 2/3 (HR < 150 bpm). The rest day on Friday provides full recovery before the long run, and the short Saturday run keeps legs moving without adding hard effort. Monitoring heart‑rate drift and subjective fatigue will confirm that the reduction is helping recovery. The long run is reduced from 20 mi to 18 mi, a realistic taper that still builds endurance but reduces the risk of over‑use injury.
